answer.rationale: The line is running at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer, so any delivery disruption is high-cost right now — this is the wrong moment to absorb switching/onboarding risk with a new primary vendor, even though the low-cost quote alone satisfies the 18% mandate. memory_c2 documents that the low-cost vendor's onboarding was quick and invoicing accurate, but it is silent on delivery reliability and lead-time performance under strain, which is exactly the dimension that matters most given the no-buffer condition — that gap is worth checking against the archived source before trusting it as a green light. memory_c4 shows that benchmarking against market quotes (like the one just received) has previously moved the incumbent meaningfully on both price and terms without any migration risk, which directly serves the 'minimize TCO without increasing delivery risk' objective. I intend to use the low-cost quote as negotiating leverage with the incumbent within the 14-day window rather than switching outright, preserving continuity while pursuing cost recovery. I'm flagging that this may not fully close the 18% gap alone, so it should be treated as this cycle's single move with vendor-switch and second-sourcing left for the next review once delivery-risk evidence on the low-cost vendor is verified.
